title: Playing a society party for Jascha Heifetz
summary: At a Palm Beach society party, Heifetz asks 'what, no violins?' and remarks that at least you can dance to jazz.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: No, he wasn't starving. I should tell you a little incident that happened down there. We played, we did play a job. They got one job for us, a one nighter at the Everglades. Vic Moore got it for us in Palm Beach and we were playing at this party, it was, you know, a society party. And we're playing jazz music and Joscho Heifetz was there with he (married?) was it Florence (Vidar?), I think Joscho Heifetz (Mary, Mary?). Anyway, we were playing jazz music for the dancing and Joscho Heifetz came up and stood there. Mr.
Heifetz is there, hello Mr. Heifetz you know. He says, what, no violins? (LAUGHTER).
He didn't know that you had thrown them away. (LAUGHTER).

We had thrown them away. I told him that I had tried to play a little violin when I was younger. But he was very nice you know. He says, it's jazz huh? Jazz. Not bad. (LAUGHTER). He says at least you can dance to it. That's about all he said. That was the finish of. it..
